passage:
Last spring the Singapore posting came through, and I spent a week pretending I could have everything. Then Trisha sat me down with a notebook. 'Jaya, write what each side is actually protecting. Plain words.'
Career: my pride in my work, the chance to learn something I can't learn here.
Family: Appa, alone in the Chennai house since Amma passed, who still forgets to eat when no one reminds him.
Seeing it written, I realised I didn't need to choose one forever. I asked for the posting to start in September instead of June. In those months my cousin agreed to move in with Appa, and we set up a Sunday video dinner.
I still lost things. I missed Appa's birthday, and the first project I'd been promised went to someone else. I chose knowing that. Pretending there was a perfect answer would have been the bigger lie.

qa.a: Appa, alone in the Chennai house since Amma passed, who still forgets to eat when no one reminds him.

qa.q: What did Jaya realise after seeing both values written down?
qa.a: Jaya realised there was no need to choose one forever and that the right order could honour both the career and Appa.

qa.q: What choice about timing did Jaya make, and what did it protect?
qa.a: Jaya moved the posting start to September, leaving time for a cousin to move in with Appa and a Sunday video dinner, so both work and family were protected.

qa.q: How might Appa experience Jaya's move with this plan in place?
qa.a: Appa would still miss Jaya, but with a cousin at home and Sunday dinners he may feel looked after rather than left alone.

grounding: Shows a young adult naming what each value protects, finding a sequence that honours both, and accepting the losses that come with the choice.

passage:
Note from Alka, head of sports, Friday
Amandeep came to my office today with the state coaching offer and a page of scribbles. He had drawn two circles, 'growth' and 'my promise'. Under growth he had written what it protects: his skill, his future, a chance to show what our programme can do. Under promise: the Sunday football group he started two years ago for children from the colony by the railway line, and their trust.
He asked me which one mattered more. I asked him instead whether there was an order that kept both alive.
Twenty minutes later he had a plan: train Rukmini from Class 12, who has helped since the start, to run Sundays; join the state camp; visit the group once a month. He said, 'I'll lose some Sundays, and some kids will be upset. I'm choosing it anyway, with my eyes open.'
I will check in with him after the first month.

qa.q: What did Amandeep write under 'my promise'?
qa.a: The Sunday football group he started two years ago for children from the colony by the railway line, and their trust.

qa.q: What did Amandeep mean by 'I'm choosing it anyway, with my eyes open'?
qa.a: He meant he knows some Sundays and some children's happiness will be lost, and he accepts that cost instead of pretending it isn't there.

qa.q: Why did Alka choose to ask about an order that kept both, instead of saying which mattered more?
qa.a: That question pushed Amandeep to build his own plan, training Rukmini, joining the camp and visiting monthly, rather than taking a ready-made verdict.

qa.q: How might the children in the Sunday group be affected by Amandeep's plan?
qa.a: Some may feel upset at seeing him less, but with Rukmini leading and monthly visits, the group keeps going and their trust is not broken.

grounding: Shows a young adult naming two values and what each protects, finding a sequence that honours both, and deciding while openly accepting some loss.
